newsitem.title: UK: GKN to bid $570 million for Sinter. [Corrected 14:30 gmt]
newsitem.headline: GKN to bid $570 million for Sinter. [Corrected 14:30 gmt]

text.p: British engineering and agriculture technology group GKN Plc said on Wednesday it planned to buy U.S. firm Sinter Metals Inc for $570 million in cash.
GKN said its bid would offer Sinter shareholders $37 per share, compared to Tuesday's closing price of $27.
GKN said shareholders representing some 43 percent of Sinter's outstanding shares had agreed to accept the offer, which was expected to close in late May.
Sinter, based in Cleveland, Ohio, makes precision, pressed- powder, metal parts and has operations in the U.S., Canada, Germany and Sweden.
GKN said it expected the acquisition, which will be paid for from company's resources, to be earnings enhancing in the first 12 months.
The bid price included $386 million for Sinter's equity and $184 million for the assumption of debt.
GKN said it would grow the enlarged business by introducing new products, expanding geographically, and making further acquisitions.
The company said output growth for the powder metallurgy industry was estimated at a compound annual rate of 11 percent in North America over the past three years and six percent in Europe.
GKN's shares jumped 30 pence to 941 by 1200 GMT.
GKN said Sinter's management would remain with the company.
Sinter had pro forma pretax profits of $24 million on pro forma sales of $373 million in 1996. (Corrects from "had pretax profits of $15 million")
Earlier this week, a newspaper reported that GKN might launch a takeover bid for Vickers Plc, despite GKN's previous dismissal of such rumours. --London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
